name: Sit a formal exam through the system, with the attempt tracked well enough to survive a dropped connection
priorityReason: A student whose connection drops mid-paper must not lose their work, and nothing else in the module protects that.

goal.capability: to sit an exam through the system without losing my work if the connection or the device fails
goal.outcome: my answers survive, my remaining time is honest, and the school can tell a completed paper from an interrupted one

secondaryActors.involvement: Authors the paper for their own subject and marks the written answers.
Assembles or reviews the paper, schedules the online exam and approves the schedule.
Releases the exam to the students' accounts. Only then does it appear to them.
Supervises the sitting where it is held on school premises.

additional.description: A student opens a released exam within its window and an attempt record is created.
The window closes and any attempt still in progress is submitted automatically (BR-8).
The window closes with a student who never opened the paper, which records them absent (BR-9).

preconditions.condition: A paper has been built from the question bank by the teacher or the Coordinator.
The Coordinator has scheduled the exam with a start and end window and a duration, and approved the schedule.
The School Admin has released it. Until then it does not appear in any student's account (BR-2).
The student is signed in to their own account.

postConditions: Every student who opened the paper holds one attempt record, carrying the start time, the elapsed time, every answer given and the state of the attempt.
Every answer was written to the attempt as it was given, so nothing depended on the student reaching the submit button.
A student whose connection dropped resumed the same attempt from the last saved answer, with the remaining time carried over from the elapsed time already recorded.
No second attempt was created for anybody, whatever happened to their device.
An attempt still in progress when the window closed was submitted automatically and marked closed by the window, so it is distinguishable from a completed submission.
A student who never opened the paper has no attempt and was recorded absent.
Objective answers were scored automatically and written answers went to the subject teacher for marking.
The marks then followed the ordinary path — grade calculation, coordinator approval and publication — with no separate route.

businessRules.rule: An online exam is a formal assessment that counts towards the result, and follows the same approval and release path as a paper exam. It is not a quiz.
The School Admin releases the exam. Only then does the paper appear in the accounts of the students it applies to, so a scheduled paper is not readable before the school intends it.
One attempt exists per student per paper. A dropped connection, a failed device or a second sign-in resumes the same attempt and never creates another.
The duration is the time one student is allowed, and may be shorter than the window. A three-hour window with a ninety-minute paper lets students start at different times.
Every answer is written to the attempt record as it is given, not only at submission. A student's work must not depend on their reaching the submit button.
On resuming, the remaining time is carried over from the elapsed time already recorded. A student who lost twenty minutes to a dead router does not also lose twenty minutes of paper.
The attempt state is one of four: in progress, submitted, closed by the window, or never attempted. Each means something different to the marker.

Where the window closes while an attempt is still in progress, the system submits it automatically with the answers saved to that point and marks it closed by the window, so it can be told apart from a completed submission.
A student who never opens the paper within the window has no attempt to submit and is recorded absent, which is then classified like any other exam absence.
Objective answers are scored automatically from the answer key; written answers go to the subject teacher for marking. A paper with both carries both.

For each online exam the Coordinator states whether it is sat on school premises under an invigilator or may be sat from home, and any restriction on the browser or device. Question order and option order are randomised per student.
The marks follow the ordinary path — grade calculation, coordinator approval and publication. An online exam produces no separate result.
Both an online exam and a quiz draw on the same single question bank. There is no separate store for multiple-choice questions.

alternateFlows.condition: The connection drops or the device fails
alternateFlows.behaviour: The student signs in again and resumes the same attempt from the last saved answer, with the remaining time carried over from the elapsed time already recorded. No new attempt is created and nothing already answered is lost (BR-3, BR-6).

alternateFlows.condition: The window closes while an attempt is in progress
alternateFlows.behaviour: The attempt is submitted automatically with the answers saved to that point and marked closed by the window, so it is distinguishable from a completed submission (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: A student never opens the paper within the window
alternateFlows.behaviour: There is no attempt to submit and the student is recorded absent, which is then classified like any other exam absence (BR-9).

alternateFlows.condition: The exam is to be sat from home
alternateFlows.behaviour: The schedule states it may be sat from home rather than under an invigilator, and any device restriction is recorded with it (BR-11).
alternateFlows.function: scheduleOnlineExam(examId, subjectId, windowOpens, windowCloses, duration, 'May be sat from home')

alternateFlows.behaviour: The whole paper is scored automatically and nothing goes to the teacher for marking (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A student signs in on a second device mid-attempt
alternateFlows.behaviour: The same attempt continues on the second device. There is one attempt per student whatever they sign in from (BR-3).

departures.requirement: Every answer is persisted as it is given. No student's work depends on reaching the submit button, on the browser closing cleanly, or on the device surviving.
There is no route by which a second attempt is created for the same student and paper, whatever device or session they sign in from.
Remaining time is calculated from elapsed time recorded server-side, so a student neither gains time by reconnecting nor loses time they did not use.
An unreleased paper is not sent to a student's account at all, rather than hidden there.
Attempts, answers and their timings are retained 7 years, matching the results calculated from them.

openQuestions.question: How is the browser or device restriction actually enforced, if at all?
openQuestions.assumption: Stated with the schedule but not enforced by anything modelled here.

openQuestions.question: What happens where a whole class loses connectivity mid-paper?
openQuestions.assumption: Each attempt resumes individually. No group extension is modelled.

openQuestions.question: May the Coordinator extend a window or a duration once the exam has started?
Is a student sitting from home identified in any way beyond their login?
openQuestions.assumption: No. This is the weakest point of a from-home sitting.

openQuestions.question: Should an attempt closed by the window be marked differently from a completed submission?
openQuestions.assumption: It is distinguishable but is marked on the same basis. Confirm the school agrees.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.
